unit: Unit 3: Accounting Standards - AS & Ind AS
learning_outcomes: Institutional framework and standard-setting authority (ICAI & MCA)
Comparison of AS vs Ind AS vs IFRS
Applicability, deferral rules, and specific mandates for the insurance sector
Conceptual differences between Indian GAAP and IFRS
key_takeaways: The Accounting Standards Board (ASB) of ICAI formulates Accounting Standards; the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) notifies them under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013.
India operates a dual accounting system: 27 active Accounting Standards (AS) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 and 39 converged Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) aligned with IFRS.
Per IRDAI directives, the implementation of Ind AS 109 and the Ind AS equivalent of IFRS 17 is deferred to roll out simultaneously; insurers presently prepare financial statements under AS only.
Insurance Mandate 1 (AS 3 - Cash Flow Statements): Insurers must prepare Cash Flow Statements using the Direct Method only.
Insurance Mandate 2 (AS 13 - Accounting for Investments): Non-life insurers are exempt from AS 13 and follow IRDAI Investment Regulations instead.
Insurance Mandate 3 (AS 17 - Segment Reporting): Mandatory for all insurance companies irrespective of listing status or turnover thresholds.
Under Indian GAAP, statutory law overrides Accounting Standards in case of conflict; IFRS prioritizes substance over legal form.
Extraordinary items are permitted and required to be shown separately under AS 5, but are strictly prohibited from separate line-item presentation under IAS 1 / Ind AS.

self_test_questions.question: Which body is responsible for formulating Accounting Standards in India?
self_test_questions.explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASB), constituted by the Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) in 1977, formulates the standards.

self_test_questions.question: Which method is mandatory for insurance companies when preparing cash flow statements under AS 3?
self_test_questions.explanation: IRDAI regulations require insurance companies to prepare cash flow statements using the Direct Method exclusively.

self_test_questions.question: Why are Indian general insurance companies currently exempt from AS 13 (Accounting for Investments)?
options: They do not hold investment portfolios
They follow separate IRDAI Investment Regulations
Investments are marked only at historical cost
self_test_questions.correct_answer: They follow separate IRDAI Investment Regulations
self_test_questions.explanation: Insurers are governed by specific IRDAI (Investment) Regulations for investment valuation and presentation rather than AS 13.

self_test_questions.question: Which standard mandates segment reporting for all insurers irrespective of listing status or turnover?
self_test_questions.explanation: AS 17 (Segment Reporting) applies compulsorily to all insurance entities regardless of size or listing criteria.

self_test_questions.question: How are extraordinary items treated under AS 5 compared to IAS 1?
options: Prohibited under AS 5, permitted under IAS 1
Permitted and disclosed separately under AS 5, prohibited under IAS 1
self_test_questions.correct_answer: Permitted and disclosed separately under AS 5, prohibited under IAS 1
self_test_questions.explanation: AS 5 requires separate disclosure of extraordinary items on the face of the P&L account, whereas IAS 1 explicitly prohibits any items from being presented as extraordinary.
